Exploit C23/C19 block-rotation symmetry (14×23+1 and 17×19) to search a tiny representative space with evolutionary hill-climbing plus soft-max Adam, then break symmetry with full-space repulsion annealing and trust-region LP polish.
direction: Search the symmetric stratum the record misses, exploiting $323 = 14\cdot23 + 1$: build configurations from 14 orbits of size 23 under block rotations by multiples of $2\pi/23$ in the three coordinate planes $(x_1x_2),(x_3x_4),(x_5x_6)$ (with rotation speeds, e.g. $(1,5,11)$ mod 23, and $x_7$ invariant), plus one pole point on the $x_7$-axis. Each orbit is then described by just a unit representative (6 free parameters), so optimise only $\sim$84 variables with derivative-free search (CMA-style random search or Nelder–Mead restarts) followed by smooth Adam on the representatives, evaluating the exact max cosine of the full 323 points; try a few speed triples and also the analogous $19$-orbit decomposition $323=17\cdot19$. Symmetry reduces the search enormously and automatically equalises contacts within orbits; LP-polish the best symmetric result in the full space, allowing symmetry to break if that helps.

idea: Escape the isostatic jam by cycling hub/rattler surgery and worst-point shakes through fast vectorized tangential hinge repulsion to change contact topology, screening each basin with a very short time-capped trust-region LP.
Large cluster surgery with joint farthest-point reinsertion, frozen-fixed softmax repulsion annealing, Metropolis acceptance, and capped trust-region LP polish.
direction: Large non-elitist cluster surgery on the incumbent: pick a hub with $\ge$18 contacts, take its contact-graph BFS neighbourhood, and delete 30–60 points consisting of that cluster plus both rattlers and the lowest-contact points; then reinsert the freed points *jointly*, not one-by-one—first place them by farthest-point sampling from 50000 random candidates against the fixed points, then run 300 steps of softmax repulsion where only freed points move (fixed points frozen), with $\tau$ annealed $10^{-2}\to10^{-3}$. Accept the result into a simulated-annealing loop even if its polished max is up to $2\times10^{-4}$ worse than the incumbent (Metropolis acceptance, temperature decaying over $\sim$120s), keeping the global best separately; finish with one capped LP polish. Deleting a whole connected cluster, rather than jittering points, is what can actually break and reform the contact graph.

Build a large lattice pool on S^6, greedily select 323 max-min points with swap search, then relax with hinge Adam and LP polish while keeping the incumbent best.
direction: Lattice/code-based combinatorial construction: generate a large structured candidate pool on $S^6$ from integer/lattice vectors—e.g. all vectors with coordinates in $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ of a few fixed squared norms (including $D_7$/$E_7$-style patterns: permutations of $(\pm1,\pm1,0^5)$, $(\pm2,0^6)$, $(\pm1^7)/\sqrt7$, half-integer vectors $(\pm1^6,\pm1)/\sqrt7$ variants)—normalised, deduplicated (tens of thousands of points). Select 323 of them by greedy max-min insertion followed by swap local search (repeatedly try replacing a selected point participating in the current maximum pair by an unselected candidate that lowers the count of near-max pairs, using simulated annealing on the number of pairs above $0.665$), then continuously relax the selected set with hinge-repulsion Adam and a final short LP polish. This tests whether an algebraic, few-distance-type configuration beats the generic jam, rather than assuming the optimum is a perturbation of it.

Force topology changes by imposing hard upper bounds max-delta on rotating matchings and hub-incident contact edges in the tangent trust-region LP, then relax the worsened state with vectorised LogSumExp tangential descent before re-polishing without forcing.
direction: Explore adjacent LP vertices by forced contact breaking: choose a matching, or a set of edges incident to overloaded hubs, and solve the usual tangent trust-region LP with the additional constraints that those selected cosines must fall to at most $\mathrm{max}-\delta$ for $\delta\in\{3\times10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3}\}$, while minimising $t$ over the remaining near-maximal pairs. Accept the resulting temporarily worse configuration, relax it with fast vectorised LogSumExp tangential descent using matrix products $G X$ rather than pair loops, and only then re-polish without the forcing constraints; systematically rotate the forced edge set so each trial deliberately destroys part of the old topology instead of relying on random kicks to do so.

idea: Replace single-point moves with connected-cluster surgery on the contact graph followed by frozen-core max-min reinsertion and short relaxations.
direction: Perform connected-cluster surgery rather than single-point surgery: build the contact graph using pairs with cosine above $\mathrm{max}-10^{-7}$, select a hub and its breadth-first neighbourhood of 12--18 points, delete that whole cluster, and reinsert the points sequentially from 50,000 random sphere candidates by max-min distance to the remaining points, followed by optimisation of only the inserted points with the core frozen and then a short all-point smooth relaxation. Cycle through several hubs and random connected clusters, keep candidates whose pre-LP max cosine is below about 0.670, LP-polish only those, snapshot the best valid array continuously, and impose a hard 165 s internal deadline.

idea: Cardinality homotopy with fast annealed soft-max repulsion and void regrowth, reserving LP for one final bounded polish.
direction: Use cardinality homotopy to create freedom absent at $N=323$: remove the 2 rattlers plus 6--14 hub or randomly chosen points, optimise the resulting $N=309$--$317$ code with annealed $p$-norm or LogSumExp repulsion until its maximum is well below the record, then regrow one point at a time by finding large spherical voids from dense candidate sampling and local max-min optimisation, allowing all points to move after each insertion. direction: Search for a structurally different, possibly more symmetric basin independently of the record: generate seeds from rotated unions of shells of $D_7$/$E_7$ lattice vectors and random finite-group orbits trimmed or padded to exactly 323 points, optimise each seed with cheap vectorised soft-max/L-BFGS dynamics on the sphere with temperature annealing, and maintain a diverse elite pool distinguished by maximum cosine and contact-graph degree distribution. Discard all but the best few distinct seeds, LP-polish only a seed whose smooth score approaches 0.665, always retain the loaded record as a fallback return value, and enforce strict wall-clock budgeting so `solve()` returns a valid array by about 170 s.

idea: Search symmetric algebraic families far from the jammed record with few-parameter cross-polytope and two-shell pools plus greedy filling and Adam polishing, falling back to the record if not better.
direction: Search a structured algebraic family far from the record instead of perturbing it. Generate candidate codes from finite coordinate patterns in $\mathbb R^7$, e.g. normalized vectors with entries in $\{0,\pm1,\pm a,\pm b\}$ or unions of orbits under cyclic/dihedral coordinate-permutation groups, choosing pattern counts summing to 323 and optimizing only the few parameters $a,b$ and orbit phases by random search plus Adam on a log-sum-exp max-cosine objective. Include patterns derived from 7D cross-polytopes, $E_7$-like root shells rescaled/rotated relative to one another, and two-shell mixtures with variable shell sizes. Free-polish only the best 3 structured candidates with gradient descent and at most one final 20s LP; this can discover a symmetric basin that unstructured noise around the record cannot reach.

idea: Shrink by 25-60 points then regrow with void-sampled max-min insertion and fast soft-max tangential annealing, using gradient steps only.
direction: Do cardinality homotopy with fast gradient methods only. Remove 25--60 points selected as rattlers plus random hub/low-contact mixtures, optimize the remaining code with batched matrix-multiplication log-sum-exp/soft-max Adam or L-BFGS at decreasing temperatures until its max cosine is clearly below $0.665$ (target $0.60$--$0.64$ for the reduced code), then reinsert points one or a few at a time by sampling 50k--200k sphere candidates, choosing max-min void points, and relaxing only the inserted points for a few hundred cheap steps before short global relaxations. Repeat insert-relax cycles until 323 points are restored, use no LP until a single final polish capped at 20--30s, and implement strict deadline checks ($<160$s total) returning the best feasible 323-point array found so far.

idea: Project random tangent kicks onto the nullspace of the contact Jacobian to get large floppy-mode steps, relax with normalized log-sum-exp repulsion, and LP-polish only topology-changed candidates.
direction: Follow floppy/null modes of the contact Jacobian before re-jamming. Build the $m\times1938$ tangent Jacobian for pairs with slack $<10^{-7}$ (rows $P_{x_i}^{\perp}x_j$ on $i$ and $P_{x_j}^{\perp}x_i$ on $j$), compute its smallest singular vectors by randomized SVD or eigendecomposition of the Gram matrix, and identify modes supported on rattlers and low-contact points. Take deliberately large steps, $0.03$--$0.20$ radians, along random combinations of 5--30 near-null modes (not gradient steps), accept only configurations whose contact graph differs by at least, say, 50 gained/lost contacts after a cheap 200-step log-sum-exp relaxation, then run one short LP polish. Enforce a hard internal deadline of 150s, check time every iteration, and always retain/return the incumbent if no accepted topology change beats it.

idea: Balanced topology-forcing Adam that breaks hub contacts with hinge slack, equalizes soft contact counts and lifts rattlers, alternating regularized exploration with pure soft-max relaxation and basin-hopping.
direction: Optimize for a balanced contact graph by breaking specified contacts rather than merely lowering the current max. Add smooth penalties that (i) reward rattlers' worst cosine approaching the global max from below, (ii) penalize variance of soft contact counts $\sum_j \sigma((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-(m-\epsilon))/\tau)$ across points, and (iii) force a rotating random subset of currently-tight edges to achieve slack at least $\delta\in[10^{-3},5\times10^{-3}]$ via hinge penalties on those pairs. Alternate 300--1000 Adam steps on this regularized/topology-forcing objective with brief pure max-cosine relaxations, accepting a new basin only if its unregularized max after relaxation is within $0.002$ of the incumbent and its contact set differs materially, then LP-polish it briefly. This directly attacks the missing property -- equitably distributed rigidity with zero rattlers and no overloaded hubs -- instead of repeatedly recreating the same unbalanced jam.
